title: Fábula

image.credit: Museo Nacional del Prado, Spain; via arthistoryproject.com

altText: A dark painting lit by a warm glow. A boy blows on a glowing ember, with a monkey beside him and a man next to them. Their faces are bright against a dark background.

source.verifiedBy: arthistoryproject.com artwork page text (title, year, medium, collection, public-domain statement)

context: An oil painting made around 1600 by El Greco, who worked in Spain, and now in the Prado Museum. The source page tags it with monkeys and chiaroscuro, the use of strong light and dark. The title Fábula means fable, and the exact meaning of the scene is open to discussion.

descriptions.k: It is dark in this picture, but a glow lights some faces. A boy blows on a tiny fire. A monkey sits close. A man is there too. Where is the light? What might they be thinking?
descriptions.g12: El Greco painted this picture around 1600. A boy blows on a glowing ember. A monkey and a man are beside him. Most of the picture is dark, but the glow makes the faces bright. What do you notice about their faces? What is happening?
descriptions.g35: Fábula was painted by El Greco around 1600 in Spain. It shows a boy blowing on a glowing ember, with a monkey and a man beside him. The background is dark, so the little glow lights their faces. This use of strong light and dark is called chiaroscuro. Look at each face and gesture. What story might the artist be inviting you to imagine?
descriptions.g68: El Greco's Fábula (c. 1600) shows a boy blowing on an ember beside a monkey and a man. Its title means fable, which hints at a story or lesson, but scholars do not agree on a single meaning. The strong contrast of light and dark, called chiaroscuro, makes the faces glow while the rest falls into shadow. How does this lighting shape the mood? What different stories could the group of figures suggest?
descriptions.g910: Fábula (c. 1600) by El Greco gathers a boy blowing on an ember, a monkey and a man in a close, dimly lit space. The title means fable, yet the exact narrative or moral is unclear and may draw on older sources. Chiaroscuro concentrates attention on faces and the small point of light. Consider how the arrangement of figures and the glow guides your reading. What interpretations does the painting support, and what limits them?
descriptions.g1112: Fábula (c. 1600) is an unusual late work in which El Greco uses a small ember to light three figures: a boy, a monkey and a man. The title invites allegorical readings, but the precise source or message is debated, and the picture may reward open reading over a single answer. Its chiaroscuro concentrates attention while leaving much in shadow. How do light, gesture and gaze produce meaning without fixed narrative, and which readings feel best supported by what is visible?

teacherNote.context: An oil painting from about 1600 by El Greco, held in the Prado Museum in Spain. The source page tags it with monkeys and chiaroscuro. The title means fable and the scene's exact meaning is debated.
directions: Have students use a flashlight in a darkened room to light a small group of objects and describe how shadows change the mood.
Ask students to write two different short stories for the painting, then point to the visual evidence for each.
Discuss why artists give works titles that suggest a story without telling it.
